text:
Predicates:
Feud(x, y) ::: x has a feud with y.
Includes(x, y) ::: x includes y.
Leads(x, y) ::: x leads y.
DiamondMine(x) ::: x is the Diamond Mine stable.
IvyNile(y) ::: y is Ivy Nile.
Imperium(x) ::: x is Imperium.
CreedBrothers(y) ::: y are the Creed Brothers.
Question:
Based on the above information, is the following statement true, false, or uncertain? Imperium doesn't have a feud with a professional wrestling stable that includes Ivy Nile.
Premises:
DiamondMine(DiamondMine) ∧ Includes(DiamondMine, CreedBrothers) ∧ Includes(DiamondMine, IvyNile) ∧ Leads(RoderickStrong, DiamondMine) ∧ Feud(Imperium, DiamondMine) ::: Diamond Mine includes the Creed Brothers and Ivy Nile, and Roderick Strong leads Diamond Mine, which has a feud with Imperium.
Conclusion:
¬Feud(Imperium, x) ∧ Includes(x, IvyNile) ::: Imperium doesn't have a feud with a stable that includes Ivy Nile.
